answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on one mechanism: every identity must bond a scarce, slashable stake before it can act. A thousand sock-puppet accounts therefore cost a thousand locked deposits, each an island of liability that cannot be withdrawn without forfeiting it. Verification forces real compute instead of cheap copying, and self-corroboration inside one's own grove of accounts scores nothing. Faking jade-grade trust thus requires paying stake, compute and slashing risk per identity, while the attacker's cost grows linearly with every fake agent it adds.
